questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to apply for exchange outside of Europe, because I see the exchange program, as a unique opportunity to go abroad and experience everyday life in a place where it might otherwise be difficult to get the opportunity to settle down. I more specifically chose the U.S., because Ive always been curious about the U.S., and even more in the times we are in now. Moreover I wanted to go somewhere where English was the first language, as I saw it as the best prerequisite for improving my own academic English. Not least, Ive heard a lot of good stuff about San Francisco, and UC Law San Francisco offered a lot of courses, which I was interested in attending.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UC Law San Francisco has been super helpful and welcoming. I was only a bit disappointed about their lack of information regarding how to waive the standard health care insurance, which is very expensive. I struggled to figure out how to waive it, and the university was not able to help me, but managed on my own hand. Moreover, I would have appreciated if the university would have told us, that all course books are available at their library. Some of the other exchange students had already bought expensive course books (which the university had strongly encouraged to do upon arrival) only to later find out that they could have managed without. Lastly, I would have appreciated the information that the visa has 1 month "grace period" after ending date. The university told me later, but by then I had already rescheduled my flight.

How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get the contact details of the landlord of a previous exchange student af UC Law San Francisco.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can save money by living off campus, but the standard will probably not be as good. However, I am glad that I chose to live off campus, since campus is located in a neighbourhood (Tenderloin), where there is a lot of homelessness, and where it can feel unsafe at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Students register through the universities portal Self Service, its quite easy, but be aware that putting courses in your calendar does not mean that you signed up for them, merely that you put them in your "shopping basket", so make sure that you did really sign up. However, the university is helpful, and helped me to get into all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange cordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the fact that you can "test" all courses in the intro week, to get a sense of the course and the professor, before making your final decision.

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was moderate, but definitely manageable. It is worth noting, that the professor and the course often matters more than the mere credits in terms of workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Attendance and participation matters.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Constitutional Law, because you get to compare different jurisdictions constitutional law, which is interesting and useful beyond the American context. Also I liked the professor -NAME REDACTED-. It is worth noting that the course focuses mostly on the human rights aspects of constitutional law, rather than institutional constitutional law. 
Intellectual Property Survey, because it gives a good introduction to intellectual property (copyright, trademark, patent and trade secrets) and the professor -NAME REDACTED- is fun.

questions.answer: Student fee (I think it was around 5,000 DKK)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out for dinner can be more affordable, than back home in Denmark, however groceries are the same level, I would say.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are good opportunities in terms of clubs, pro bono etc. However, there were no sport opportunities beside the run club which I attended. So dont expect a sport opportunities like on bigger U.S. campuses, but there are a lot of other fun clubs that you can join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host institution offered social activities for the exchange students together with the L.L.M. students, which has been super nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Check out the "fun and cheap in San Francisco" website to see events happening in the city. There are always a lot of interesting cultural events going on and its a nice way to get to know the city. Go travel with some other exchange and L.L.M. students even if just for a day or a weekend trip, there is so many nice things to see in California.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed camping in the many national parks, which were incredible, and had a super nice trip down the coast to Los Angeles. Also Las Vegas was fun to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not too bad.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the students in your courses they are super nice and welcoming and join some of the many clubs that the university has.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The "office hours" and the students relationship to their professors, which is very unlike the one we have to our teachers back home in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Because San Francisco people are super welcoming and talkative I very rarely felt homesick

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The city, the people and the weather has been wonderful!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic culture

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I dont think so

questions.answer: Yes
